answer: Harbor clerks used to stamp any skiff as a fishing co-op, so 20 sister hulls drained one subsidy. Now a berth pays only when a skipper holds a 4-hour zenith sun fix, pumps 180 L from an oasis tank through a 2.1 m salinity cell, and logs a 37-minute ocean current transect into a 12-bin shear map, locking 30 POA for 6 epochs. Three surveyors rebuild that map in 1.1 s and must match a 0.8 ppt salinity band plus a 14 cm draft stripe. One key may berth 1 hull each epoch, so 25 aliases lock 750 POA. A reused cell serial, or two maps sharing 9 of 12 bins, burns 13 POA and bars that key for 4 epochs.
